payload.rationale: Denver hosts Jacksonville at Empower Field, where altitude and crowd give the Broncos one of the stronger home-field edges in the league (roughly 2.5–3 points, worth about 8–10 percentage points of win probability versus a neutral site). Background knowledge: both clubs were playoff-caliber in 2025, with Denver's defense and Bo Nix's development making them a consensus top AFC team entering 2026, and Jacksonville having taken a large step forward under Liam Coen and Trevor Lawrence. On prior strength I would view these teams as roughly comparable, perhaps a slight Denver edge, which at home translates to about 60% for Denver. Week 1 results (Jaguars +24 margin, Broncos -21 margin) are a very small, opponent-unadjusted sample; they nudge the estimate a few points toward Jacksonville but should not dominate a preseason prior. Denver's injury report is minor (WR Marvin Mims Jr. out, RB RJ Harvey questionable), while Jacksonville is fully healthy, a small additional tilt toward Jacksonville. Netting these, I estimate Denver at about 58%. Too high: if Denver's Week 1 blowout loss reflects real regression (e.g., offensive line or QB issues) and Jacksonville's win reflects genuine improvement, the Jaguars could be the better team even on the road, pushing Denver below 50%. Too low: if Week 1 was noise and Denver's 2025 defense remains elite, the home altitude edge could make Denver a solid ~65% favorite. Ties (~0.4%) are excluded from the win event.
limitations: Only one game of 2026 data; Week 1 margins are not opponent-adjusted.
No final inactive lists or confirmation of Week 1 opponents/quality supplied.
Estimate relies on background priors about 2025 team strength that may not carry over to 2026 rosters and coaching.
No fitted model; subjective judgment on home-field magnitude and prior strength.
